heading: Read first: seven bounded inspection commands
introduction: For every card, open the authorized FortiGate CLI console or approved terminal session before typing. Confirm the device and required administrative context with its owner; these are not PC-shell commands. Use documentation for the installed build. Read-only here means no intentional configuration change, not zero processing cost.
privacyNote: Outputs can contain serial numbers, addresses, names and sensitive script content. Keep the original evidence private and share only reviewed, redacted excerpts. These commands do not enable continuous debugging. Do not clear logs or run an automation test as part of inspection.

checks.purpose: FortiGate: record identity, build and restart classification
checks.observation: Record the version/build and available last-reboot information with the observation time. Remove private identifiers from shared copies.
checks.limit: A warm reboot does not identify the particular action or rule. This status snapshot is not a complete incident timeline or hardware health certificate.
checks.stop: This is a finite status display. Finish at the prompt; do not issue a restart to create a new sample. Retain the original observation privately.

checks.observation: Compare the incident timestamps and process names, including autod when present, with the System Events and actual stitch configuration.
checks.limit: Process or interface-down entries do not alone prove causation. Missing entries may reflect retention or an incomplete record, not a clean bill of health.
checks.stop: Read the finite saved history and stop when the prompt returns. Do not clear the crashlog, enable debug, or treat the command name as permission to run tests.

checks.purpose: FortiGate: inspect stitch references and targets
checks.observation: Identify the relevant stitch, referenced trigger, action entries and destinations. Confirm omitted defaults through build-specific help and the authorized administrator.
checks.limit: Configuration establishes a possible execution path, not proof that it ran. Do not equate an absent non-default line with a disabled setting.
checks.stop: This command only displays configuration. Finish at the prompt without entering config mode or clicking Test in the automation interface.

checks.observation: Find the trigger referenced by the suspect stitch and compare its condition with the actual incident event. Check the installed build's supported event types.
checks.limit: A similar trigger name is not an exact match. A configured update-related trigger does not prove every update check causes an execution.
checks.stop: Read and record only the relevant sanitized excerpt. Do not change the trigger or simulate an event merely to make the timeline fit.

checks.purpose: FortiGate: inspect action type and script content
checks.observation: Read the exact referenced action. Inspect native system actions and CLI scripts, plus privilege and destination dependencies where applicable.
checks.limit: Reading an action is not executing it, and the action name alone does not describe its behavior. Shared definitions may affect multiple stitches.
checks.stop: Finish the display and protect any sensitive script output. Do not copy the script into the console or invoke Test to verify a reboot action.

checks.observation: Record enabled state, frequency and time settings. Interpret them using the installed build, timezone and observed update history.
checks.limit: Schedule configuration is not proof of a successful update or an exact reboot interval. Existing settings may differ from a release's defaults.
checks.stop: Read the display without entering the configuration block. Do not disable updates or reduce their frequency to hide the unintended action.

checks.purpose: FortiGate: distinguish update attempts from installations
checks.observation: Record relevant database versions, last installed update, last attempt and result. Compare these times with the automation and reboot records.
checks.limit: An attempt is not a successful installation. No Updates can mean nothing new was available; this output alone does not establish business-service health.
checks.stop: Finish at the prompt and retain a redacted record. Do not force an update or run an automation action just to obtain a desired result.
